newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE BOARD AGREES TO LONGER TRADING HOURS.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE BOARD AGREES TO LONGER TRADING HOURS.

text.p: The suprevisory board of the Warsaw Stock Exchange (WSE) studied a proposal of changes in the bourse's trading hours and voiced no objections, the board said in statement on Wednesday.
Earlier the Warsaw bourse's management proposed that trade begin half an hour earlier and end half an hour later than at present.
It also suggested to brokerage houses that continuous trade begin after the regular single price auction session ends instead of the two running concurrently.
According to the proposal, the regular bourse session would begin at 1030 local time and end at 1200, when continuous trade would begin. Continuous trade would end at 1330 local time.
Continuous prices would be allowed to fluctuate in relation to their same-day fixing prices rather than the previous day's as it is the case now.
